key_insight: Gan Jiang is a self-learning X-ray diffraction agent that turns failed analyses into reusable, validated skills for phase identification and whole-pattern modeling without retraining the language model.
engineering_relevance: This work shows how an integrated scientific tool ecosystem can automate and improve diffraction-based materials characterization across diverse experimental settings, from batteries to catalysts to cultural heritage samples.
method: Combines XMatcher, XQueryer, XDecomposer, and WPEM for phase ID, multiphase decomposition, and physics-constrained refinement.
Diagnoses analysis failures, revises skill instructions/code, and validates fixes before reusing them.
Freezes improved skills after development-data selection to benchmark against expert-designed workflows.
evidence_signal: On DeltaXRDbench, the agent outperformed comparators in single- and multiphase identification, and on MP500/RRUFF/opXRD it reached top-1 single-phase accuracies of 96.30%, 81.78%, and 40.83% without supplied composition.
watch_item: Performance depends on a curated tool ecosystem and validated skill updates, so robustness may vary when models, instruments, or diffraction domains fall outside the tested benchmarks.
paper_title: A self-learning scientific agent for X-ray diffraction
